description: Here, we aim to train and raise young astronauts together, exploring space and establishing life there with them. On this journey, we follow a determined path and take firm steps.
summary: This project aims to design a training capsule tailored for young astronaut candidates. It is engineered to simulate critical operational challenges in space, with environmental conditions meticulously accounted for. Furthermore, anomalous and hazardous scenarios—such as unexpected system failures, critical accidents, and microgravity environments that deviate from standard living conditions—are comprehensively integrated into the simulation framework..
details:
What is its purpose and how does it work?

Project Butterfly is a pre-training simulation capsule designed to allow astronaut candidates to acclimate to real-life space conditions, daily routines, and potential crisis moments before spaceflight. Unlike the complex and artificial-feeling rope mechanisms in existing training systems, we offer a much more natural, streamlined, and realistic atmosphere. Thanks to the smart mechanical balance and vibration infrastructure within the capsule, candidates experience the sensation of low gravity while directly confronting unexpected scenarios such as launch vibrations, sudden lighting failures, and power outages.

What was used during the development process?

While developing the project, we avoided complex software or artificial virtual reality headsets, focusing entirely on physical reality and a robust hardware architecture. Aluminum profiles were chosen for the lightweight and durable main skeleton of the capsule, and transparent polycarbonate sheets were selected to allow safe observation of the candidate inside. Linear electromagnetic motors were utilized to provide the sensation of vibration and movement, alongside high-current relays and RGB lighting systems to create sudden power interruptions and emergency atmospheres. Additionally, pressurized liquid containers and an ergonomic astronaut seat featuring a 5-point safety harness were integrated into the system for daily life testing.

How creative is the project, and which factors were considered during development?

The most fundamental feature that makes Project Butterfly creative is that it removes space training from the monopoly of massive, complex mechanical systems, transforming it into a human-centric and accessible capsule experience. Throughout the design process, we primarily focused on human psychology, physical safety, and realism. By eliminating the artificiality caused by complex ropes, we prioritized enabling candidates to feel genuinely inside a spacecraft and develop muscle memory through natural means.
